skill.name: distributed-debugging-debug-trace
skill.description: Configure distributed debugging, tracing, profiling, logging, and diagnostics workflows for multi-service systems.
skill.summary: Set up safe debug and trace workflows for distributed applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static command, environment, and certificate findings are false positives from JavaScript template literals, Markdown formatting, or safe configuration reads. I confirmed unsafe examples for open remote debugging, DOM injection, WebSocket debug streaming, filesystem profile dumps, and full request-body telemetry. The playbook should be hardened before publication because copied examples can expose code execution, sensitive diagnostics, and personal data.

remediation.issue: Remote debug evaluation accepts expressions over a WebSocket flow without authentication in the sample.
remediation.suggestion: Bind debug listeners to localhost by default, require strong authentication, enforce TLS, and remove Runtime.evaluate from remotely reachable paths.

remediation.issue: Examples bind Node inspector and debug ports to 0.0.0.0.
remediation.suggestion: Use localhost defaults, document SSH tunnels or VPN-only access, and require explicit user confirmation before exposing debug ports.

remediation.issue: Tracing examples capture full request bodies and user or session identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Redact request bodies by default, allowlist safe span attributes, and hash or omit user and session identifiers.

remediation.issue: Debug dashboard examples render trace and log data with innerHTML.
remediation.suggestion: Render dynamic dashboard values with textContent or a trusted sanitizer, and validate class names before applying them.

remediation.issue: Profiling examples write CPU profiles and heap snapshots to disk.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output directories, protect diagnostic files, set retention limits, and document cleanup procedures for sensitive snapshots.

content.value_statement: Distributed systems hide failures across services, logs, and traces. This skill helps teams configure debugging, tracing, profiling, and safe diagnostics workflows.
actual_capabilities: Plans local and remote debugging workflows for Node.js and browser applications.
Defines OpenTelemetry tracing setup, span boundaries, and correlation fields.
Creates structured logging guidance with service metadata and log levels.
Outlines profiling, heap snapshot, and memory monitoring workflows.
Provides dashboard and production debugging patterns with safety cautions.
limitations: The skill provides patterns and examples, not a complete observability platform.
Examples require security review before production use.
Tooling choices may need changes for non-Node.js stacks.
It cannot inspect live systems unless the user supplies context and access.

use_cases.title: Trace A Multi-Service Failure
use_cases.description: Map service boundaries, add trace context, and identify missing spans across a request path.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Debugging
use_cases.description: Create shared logging, source map, and debugger setup guidance for development teams.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Production Latency
use_cases.description: Design guarded profiling, sampling, and dashboard workflows for a live incident.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Debug Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a service with unclear failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a debugging plan for my service. Ask for the runtime, failure symptoms, logs, and deployment environment.

prompt_templates.title: Add Distributed Tracing
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate tracing setup across several services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a distributed tracing setup for these services. Include span boundaries, correlation fields, sampling, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Production Diagnostics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this production debugging workflow. Identify security risks, redaction needs, access controls, and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate An Incident
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incident workflow with traces, logs, and profiles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an incident debugging plan using traces, logs, metrics, heap snapshots, and profiling. Include decision points and rollback criteria.

output_examples.input: A checkout request is slow across three services.
output_examples.output: A trace plan that names each service boundary, required correlation fields, sampling settings, and checks for missing spans.

output_examples.input: A production API has intermittent memory growth.
output_examples.output: A guarded profiling workflow with access controls, snapshot handling rules, and cleanup steps for sensitive diagnostic files.

output_examples.input: A team needs consistent debug logs.
output_examples.output: A logging standard with levels, service metadata, trace identifiers, retention guidance, and redaction rules.

best_practices: Bind debug interfaces to localhost unless a reviewed access-control plan exists.
Redact request bodies, session identifiers, tokens, and personal data before tracing or logging.
Set sampling, retention, and cleanup rules before enabling profiling or heap snapshots.
anti_patterns: Expose remote debuggers on all network interfaces without authentication.
Store full request bodies or user sessions in spans and logs.
Render debug dashboard data with unsafe HTML insertion.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure debugging, tracing, logging, profiling, dashboards, and production diagnostic workflows.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy every example directly?
faq.answer: No. Some examples need authentication, redaction, and network restrictions before production use.

faq.question: Does it support OpenTelemetry?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes OpenTelemetry setup patterns and guidance for spans and resource attributes.

faq.question: Can it help with production incidents?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure incident debugging plans with traces, logs, profiles, and rollback criteria.

faq.question: Does it replace an observability vendor?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance that can work with existing tracing, logging, and monitoring tools.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Provide service names, runtimes, deployment details, failure symptoms, logs, metrics, and security constraints.
